papers.title: Leveraging serum CHI3L1 and machine learning for non-invasive liver fibrosis diagnostics.
papers.abstract: This study was aimed to develop non-invasive liver fibrosis diagnostic model using chitinase 3-like protein 1 (CHI3L1) based on machine learning (ML).1,011 follow-up patients (556 training/455 validation) were enrolled, staging fibrosis via transient elastography (F01, F2, F23, F34, and F4). Demographic, clinical, and laboratory parameters were collected. Fibrosis-related indicators were selected by differential analysis and correlation analysis. ML models were developed, optimized, and validated. Of 23 initial laboratory indicators, 15 indicators were selected to developed a 5-stage liver fib
papers.summary: This study developed machine learning models that use serum CHI3L1 along with routine clinical and laboratory indicators to non-invasively stage liver fibrosis in 1,011 follow-up patients, validated against transient elastography. The models distinguish five fibrosis stages (F01–F4), suggesting CHI3L1 could improve non-invasive fibrosis diagnostics over existing approaches.

papers.title: Genomic language model for predicting enhancers and their allele-specific activity in the human genome.
papers.abstract: Predicting and deciphering the regulatory logic of enhancers remains a significant challenge due to their complex sequence features and the absence of consistent genetic or epigenetic signatures that distinguish them from other genomic regions. Existing machine learning methods capture nucleotide composition but often fail to model sequence context effectively.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a genomic language model designed to predict enhancer regions and their allele-specific activity directly from human genome sequence. By leveraging sequence context modeling, the approach aims to overcome limitations of prior machine learning methods that rely mainly on nucleotide composition and struggle to capture regulatory logic. The model offers a new way to identify enhancers and assess how genetic variants affect their function.

papers.title: De novo Genes in Plants: Origins, Mechanisms, and Functional Implications.
papers.abstract: De novo genes originate from previously non-coding genomic regions. They provide an important source of lineage-specific innovation. In plants, these genes may contribute to adaptation, trait diversity and crop evolution. This review summarizes recent progress in plant de novo gene research. It first discusses major routes of gene birth, including transcription-first, open reading frame (ORF)-first and concurrent models. It also examines how nascent loci acquire regulatory control and enter existing biological networks. The review then summarizes their evolutionary features, including weak ear
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent research on de novo genes in plants, which arise from previously non-coding genomic regions and serve as a source of lineage-specific innovation. It covers the major models of gene birth (transcription-first, ORF-first, and concurrent), how nascent loci acquire regulatory control and integrate into biological networks, and their evolutionary features. The review highlights the potential contributions of these genes to plant adaptation, trait diversity, and crop evolution.

papers.title: Gradient-based Optimization for mRNA Sequence Design.
papers.abstract: Designing mRNA coding sequences that simultaneously optimize RNA accessibility in the translation initiation region and codon adaptation while preserving the encoded protein requires navigating a vast discrete combinatorial space. The inherently discrete nature of codon choices prevents direct application of gradient-based optimization, despite the availability of accurate deep learning predictors such as DeepRaccess for RNA accessibility prediction.
papers.summary: This paper presents a gradient-based optimization approach for designing mRNA coding sequences that balance RNA accessibility in the translation initiation region with codon adaptation, while keeping the encoded protein unchanged. The key challenge addressed is that codon choices are discrete, which normally prevents gradient-based methods, despite the availability of accurate deep learning predictors like DeepRaccess.

papers.title: Quantitative mapping from conventional MRI using self-supervised physics-guided deep learning: Applications to a large-scale, clinically heterogeneous dataset.
papers.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a cornerstone of clinical neuroimaging, yet conventional MRIs provide qualitative information heavily dependent on scanner hardware and acquisition settings. While quantitative MRI (qMRI) offers intrinsic tissue parameters, the requirement for specialized acquisition protocols and reconstruction algorithms restricts its availability and impedes large-scale biomarker research. This study presents a self-supervised physics-guided deep learning framework to infer quantitative T1, T2, and proton-density (PD) maps directly from widely available clinical conventio
papers.summary: This study introduces a self-supervised, physics-guided deep learning framework that infers quantitative T1, T2, and proton-density maps directly from conventional clinical MRI scans, avoiding the need for specialized acquisition protocols. The approach is validated on a large-scale, clinically heterogeneous dataset, suggesting it could enable quantitative biomarker research using existing MRI archives.

papers.title: A Novel Unsupervised Learning Model with Bayesian Hyperparameter Optimization for Predicting Substrates of Promiscuous Enzymes.
papers.abstract: Promiscuous enzymes catalyze multiple biochemical reactions, but predicting their substrate profiles remains challenging because annotations are incomplete, reliable negative labels are scarce, and enzyme-substrate relationships are inherently multilabel. Here, we present PreSEPM (Predictive Substrate Explorer for Promiscuous Enzymes), a sequence-only, closed-set framework that combines pretrained protein representations, Gaussian mixture modeling, cluster-substrate alignment, and Bayesian optimization of decision thresholds. PreSEPM operates within a predefined substrate panel and does not re
papers.summary: The authors present PreSEPM, an unsupervised machine learning framework that predicts which substrates a promiscuous enzyme can act on using only its protein sequence. It combines pretrained protein representations, Gaussian mixture modeling, cluster-substrate alignment, and Bayesian optimization of decision thresholds to handle multilabel enzyme-substrate relationships without needing reliable negative labels.

papers.title: Humanizing Antibodies and Nanobodies From Scratch With HuDiff.
papers.abstract: Antibody (Ab) and nanobody (Nb) humanization is essential for reducing immunogenicity in therapeutic applications. HuDiff is an adaptive autoregressive diffusion approach that generates humanized antibodies and nanobodies from scratch using only complementarity-determining region sequences as input, eliminating the need for preexisting human templates. The method follows a two-stage training pipeline: pretraining on human antibody sequences to learn framework region patterns, followed by fine-tuning on target-species sequences. HuDiff-Ab processes paired heavy and light chains for conventional
papers.summary: HuDiff is a new adaptive autoregressive diffusion method that humanizes antibodies and nanobodies using only complementarity-determining region sequences, without requiring preexisting human templates. It uses a two-stage training pipeline—pretraining on human antibody sequences to learn framework patterns, then fine-tuning on target-species sequences—and handles paired heavy/light chains for conventional antibodies.

papers.title: PMPIHGLL: predicting metabolite-protein interactions using dual hypergraph convolutional networks and large language models.
papers.abstract: Metabolite-protein interactions (MPIs) play pivotal roles in regulating cellular processes and metabolic pathways and have important implications for systems biology and drug discovery. Although several computational models have been proposed, alternative approaches are needed to broaden the methodological toolkit for MPI prediction. In this study, we developed a new deep-learning model for predicting MPIs. Chemical and protein large language models were used to generate informative representations of metabolites and proteins. For each entity type, we constructed two K-nearest-neighbor hypergr
papers.summary: The authors present PMPIHGLL, a deep-learning model that predicts metabolite-protein interactions by combining chemical and protein large language models with dual hypergraph convolutional networks. The approach generates informative representations of metabolites and proteins and captures higher-order relationships via K-nearest-neighbor hypergraphs. This expands the computational toolkit for MPI prediction, with relevance to systems biology and drug discovery.

papers.title: Long-read based detection of large copy number variants with potential functional significance using the ContextSV structural variant caller.
papers.abstract: Long-read sequencing enables improved detection of structural variants (SVs) in the human genome due to its substantially increased read lengths. However, currently widely used long-read SV callers primarily rely on alignment-based evidence, limiting their ability to detect large and complex SVs and potentially missing disease-relevant events. To address these limitations, we developed ContextSV, a framework that integrates alignment evidence with copy number predictions derived from sequencing coverage and single-nucleotide variant allele frequencies to improve SV detection, particularly for
papers.summary: ContextSV is a new structural variant caller for long-read sequencing that combines alignment-based evidence with copy number predictions from sequencing coverage and SNV allele frequencies. This hybrid approach improves detection of large and complex copy number variants that are often missed by standard alignment-based callers, potentially capturing disease-relevant events.

papers.title: CCT2 defines a highly cisplatin-resistant and poor-prognosis subtype of lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Cisplatin-based chemotherapy is a standard treatment for lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), yet acquired cisplatin resistance remains a marked cause of treatment failure. The molecular mechanisms driving cisplatin resistance in LUAD have not been fully elucidated. The present study integrated bulk transcriptomic data, genomic mutation profiles and single-cell RNA sequencing data to systematically investigate cisplatin resistance in LUAD. Resistance-associated genes were identified through differential expression, survival analysis and database integration. Unsupervised clustering was used to define c
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomics, mutation data, and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify genes driving cisplatin resistance in lung adenocarcinoma, pinpointing CCT2 as a marker of a highly resistant, poor-prognosis subtype. Unsupervised clustering based on resistance-associated genes defines patient subgroups with distinct outcomes, suggesting CCT2 could serve as a prognostic biomarker or therapeutic target.

papers.title: An O-glycosylation-based prognostic signature for biochemical recurrence in prostate cancer identifies GALNTL6 as a potential promoter of malignant phenotypes.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is frequently diagnosed in men, and biochemical recurrence (BCR) remains a persistent problem after clinical treatment. Commonly used indicators do not identify patients who are likely to relapse early. Protein O-linked glycosylation is an important post-translational modification involved in cancer progression, but its prognostic relevance and regulatory mechanisms in PCa remain insufficiently understood. GALNTL6, which encodes polypeptide N-acetylgalactosaminyltransferase-like 6, is putatively involved in mucin-type protein O-linked glycosylation and remains poorly char
papers.summary: This study developed a prognostic signature for biochemical recurrence in prostate cancer based on O-glycosylation-related genes, and identified GALNTL6 as a potential driver of malignant phenotypes. The findings suggest that O-glycosylation patterns could help identify patients at risk of early relapse and that GALNTL6 may serve as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptome analysis and machine learning to construct a homeostatic model of acetylation for bladder cancer and validate the key gene CES1.
papers.abstract: Bladder cancer (BLCA) is one of the most common malignant tumors of the urinary system. Protein acetylation (PA) plays a critical role in regulating multiple biological processes (BPs), cellular homeostasis, and cancer-related signaling pathways. This study aimed to construct a homeostatic model of acetylation for BLCA using integrated transcriptome analysis and machine learning and to validate the key gene CES1.
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptome data with machine learning to build a homeostatic model of protein acetylation in bladder cancer, aiming to identify acetylation-related genes with prognostic or functional relevance. The authors validate CES1 as a key gene within this model, suggesting it plays a role in bladder cancer biology. The work provides a computational framework and a candidate gene for further investigation in bladder cancer.

papers.title: CCNA2 orchestrates the PI3K/AKT signaling axis to propel prostate cancer metastasis.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) remains one of the most common malignancies in men, posing a persistent global burden in terms of both public health and socioeconomic costs. Although early detection is essential for improving patient outcomes, existing clinical tools, including prostate-specific antigen (PSA) screening, digital rectal examination, and transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy, are hampered by suboptimal specificity and positive predictive value, resulting in frequent overdiagnosis and overtreatment of indolent lesions while missing a subset of aggressive tumors at an early stage. In this con
papers.summary: This study identifies CCNA2 (cyclin A2) as a driver of prostate cancer metastasis through activation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. The findings suggest that CCNA2 could serve as a potential biomarker or therapeutic target to distinguish aggressive tumors from indolent lesions, addressing a key limitation of current PSA-based screening.

papers.title: Machine learning-based prediction and external validation of treatment-related myelosuppression in patients with non-small cell lung cancer receiving PD-1 inhibitors plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy.
papers.abstract: The application of programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitors combined with platinum-based double-drug chemotherapy in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is becoming increasingly widespread. However, the impact of this treatment regimen on the bone marrow hematopoietic system is well-defined. Therefore, we have to consider the risk of bone marrow suppression in NSCLC patients after receiving this treatment regimen. Our objective was to identify risk factors for the risk of myelosuppression, one of the serious complications of PD-1 inhibitor plus platinum-based dual-agent c
papers.summary: This study developed machine learning models to predict treatment-related myelosuppression in NSCLC patients receiving PD-1 inhibitors plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy, and validated the models in an external cohort. The work identifies risk factors for this serious hematologic complication and demonstrates the potential of ML-based risk stratification to guide clinical monitoring.

papers.title: Investigating the mechanisms of PhIP-induced colorectal cancer through network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular dynamics simulation.
papers.abstract: Over the past few years, 2-amino-1-methyl-6-phenylimidazo[4,5-b]pyridine (PhIP)- a compound from grilled or processed meats-has emerged as a major player in cancer development, especially colorectal cancer (CRC). This work dives into its potential links to CRC and uncovers the key genes that bridge this connection.
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular dynamics simulations to identify key genes linking the dietary carcinogen PhIP (found in grilled and processed meats) to colorectal cancer. The work aims to uncover molecular mechanisms by which PhIP exposure may promote CRC development.

papers.title: Development and internal validation of an interpretable machine learning prognostic prediction model for postoperative delirium after esophagectomy.
papers.abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent neurological complication associated with adverse outcomes after esophagectomy. Existing risk-assessment tools may provide limited individualized prognostic information. This study aimed to develop and internally validate an interpretable machine learning (ML) prognostic prediction model for POD after esophagectomy.
papers.summary: This study developed and internally validated an interpretable machine learning model to predict postoperative delirium in patients undergoing esophagectomy, a common and serious neurological complication. The model aims to provide more individualized risk assessment than existing tools, though validation was limited to the same cohort.

papers.title: Plasma Metabolites for Identifying Bacterial Infection in Acute-on-chronic Liver Failure: A Prospective Multicenter Study.
papers.abstract: Bacterial infection is a key cause of mortality in patients with acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF). In this study, we aimed to identify metabolite biomarkers and develop a novel machine learning model for early identification of bacterial infection in ACLF.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical and translational hepatology
papers.summary: This prospective multicenter study aimed to identify plasma metabolite biomarkers and develop a machine learning model for early detection of bacterial infection in patients with acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF). The work addresses a clinically important diagnostic gap, since bacterial infection is a major driver of mortality in this population.

papers.title: Integrative Multi-omics and Machine Learning Reveal the Therapeutic Mechanisms of Juanyu-Xiaozhi Formula in Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Hepatic Fibrosis via the AP-1/PPARγ/SCD1 Axis.
papers.abstract: Despite the surging global prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and related liver fibrosis, effective treatments remain limited. While the traditional Chinese medicine Juanyu-Xiaozhi Formula (JYXZF) is used against MASLD, its bioactive components and mechanisms are poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of JYXZF and elucidate its underlying mechanisms of action.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical and translational hepatology
papers.summary: This study combines multi-omics profiling with machine learning to identify the active components and mechanisms of the traditional Chinese medicine formula Juanyu-Xiaozhi in treating metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and liver fibrosis. The authors identify an AP-1/PPARγ/SCD1 signaling axis as a key mediator of the formula's therapeutic effects. The work provides a mechanistic rationale for a traditional herbal formula using modern computational and omics approaches.

papers.title: Dynamics-aware geometric learning predicts disease-associated molecular perturbations.
papers.abstract: Missense mutations and post-translational modifications (PTMs) are major molecular perturbations that reshape protein function but are traditionally studied independently. Current computational approaches largely rely on sequence conservation or static structural features, limiting our understanding of how perturbations alter intrinsic protein dynamics. We present DynGeo-Pheno, a unified geometric deep learning framework that integrates protein language model representations with anisotropic network model-derived dynamics to jointly capture evolutionary, structural, and biophysical information
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present DynGeo-Pheno, a geometric deep learning framework that combines protein language model embeddings with anisotropic network model-derived dynamics to predict how missense mutations and post-translational modifications perturb protein function. By jointly modeling evolutionary, structural, and dynamic information rather than relying on static features alone, the method aims to capture how molecular perturbations reshape intrinsic protein dynamics.

papers.title: Integrating single-cell transcriptomics to construct an oncogene-driven prognostic model and elucidate metabolic-immune crosstalk in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related deaths, its progression and treatment heterogeneity are mainly influenced by driver gene and tumor micro-environment (TME) interactions. Nevertheless, the mechanisms of this process at the single-cell level remain unclear. This study integrated TCGA and multi-center single-cell transcriptome data to identify a 575 genes HCC-specific core set, developing a single-cell "oncogene scoring" system to quantify individual carcinogenic activity. This score is significantly elevated in malignant and proliferative T cells and is closely
papers.summary: This study integrates TCGA bulk data with multi-center single-cell transcriptome data to define a 575-gene HCC-specific core set and build a single-cell 'oncogene scoring' system that quantifies carcinogenic activity per cell. The score is elevated in malignant and proliferative T cells and is used to construct a prognostic model and explore metabolic-immune crosstalk in the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: BeitAI-pHLA: Multiallele Peptide-HLA Class I Binding Prediction Using Protein Language Model and Multi-Instance Learning.
papers.abstract: Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules participate in cellular immune responses by binding to peptide fragments derived from antigens. Exploring this process is crucial to understanding the mechanisms and underlying factors that regulate the cellular immune system. Due to the extreme polymorphism of HLA, the peptides obtained from mass spectrometry of eluted ligand experiments typically correspond to multiple HLA alleles. They are thus poly-specific, providing various options for HLA assignments. This introduces notable challenges for accurate peptide-HLA assignment and interpretation. To add
papers.summary: BeitAI-pHLA is a new computational method for predicting whether peptides bind to class I HLA molecules, using a protein language model combined with multi-instance learning to handle the common situation where mass spectrometry experiments yield peptides that could match multiple HLA alleles. This addresses a key challenge in immunopeptidomics, where peptide-HLA assignments are ambiguous due to HLA polymorphism. The approach aims to improve accuracy in identifying which peptides bind which HLA variants, with implications for vaccine design and immunotherapy.

papers.title: Development and validation of machine learning models for 30-day mortality prediction in septic shock.
papers.abstract: Septic shock carries a high risk of death, yet traditional prognostic tools have limitations. This study aimed to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models for predicting 30-day mortality in septic shock patients using comprehensive admission variables.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates machine learning models to predict 30-day mortality in patients with septic shock using comprehensive admission variables. The work aims to improve on traditional prognostic tools, which have known limitations, by leveraging ML approaches for risk stratification.

papers.title: DBP-CanPred: a machine learning model for predicting cancer-causing mutations in DNA-binding proteins.
papers.abstract: The fundamental cellular processes, including transcriptional regulation, chromatin organization, and genome maintenance, are regulated by DNA-binding proteins (DBPs). Mutations in DBPs can alter protein-DNA interactions, leading to tumor development. However, identifying such driver mutations remains a major challenge due to limitations of experimental approaches.
papers.summary: DBP-CanPred is a machine learning model designed to predict cancer-causing mutations specifically in DNA-binding proteins, addressing the gap left by experimental methods that are costly and low-throughput. It leverages features of protein-DNA interactions to classify driver mutations, potentially aiding in the prioritization of cancer variants for further study.

papers.title: Study of deep learning cues for cross linguistic part of speech tagging in English- Malayalam code-mixed data.
papers.abstract: Part Of Speech (POS) tagging is a fundamental task in Natural Language Processing (NLP) that assigns grammatical labels to words in a sentence. Code mixed text, which entails switching between two or more languages within a single conversation or a sentence, presents challenges for POS tagging. This investigation entailed a comprehensive study of deep learning approaches for cross linguistic POS tagging, focused on English Malayalam code mixed data prevalent on social media platforms. The study was carried out on linguistically complex and varied English Malayalam code mixed text from social m
papers.summary: This study evaluates deep learning approaches for part-of-speech tagging on English-Malayalam code-mixed social media text, a linguistically challenging setting where speakers switch languages within sentences. It provides a comparative analysis of neural architectures and cues for handling cross-linguistic tagging in this low-resource, code-mixed context.

papers.title: Predicting food taste with bound-driven optimization.
papers.abstract: The prediction of sensory attributes from ingredient-level formulations is an emerging challenge at the intersection of food science and artificial intelligence. We address the fundamental question of whether the taste of a food can be predicted from its ingredients by treating recipes as composite materials. We apply Hashin-Shtrikman (HS) and Reuss-Voigt (RV) bounds, techniques originally developed for elastic moduli, as a null-hypothesis additive baseline for five taste dimensions (sweetness, sourness, bitterness, umami, saltiness) on a curated dataset of 70 recipes decomposed into 115 disti
papers.summary: This study tests whether the taste of a food can be predicted from its ingredient composition by borrowing bounds from materials science (Hashin-Shtrikman and Reuss-Voigt) as an additive baseline for five taste dimensions. Using a curated dataset of 70 recipes decomposed into 115 distinct ingredients, the authors show that these physics-inspired bounds provide a useful null model for taste prediction.

papers.title: Discovery and validation of a multi-protein panel for predicting non-fatal major adverse cardiovascular events in diabetic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: To identify plasma protein biomarkers associated with incident non-fatal major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in diabetic kidney disease (DKD) patients.
papers.summary: This study identifies and validates a panel of plasma proteins that can predict non-fatal major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with diabetic kidney disease. Using proteomic profiling, the authors discovered candidate biomarkers and confirmed their predictive value in an independent cohort, offering a potential tool for cardiovascular risk stratification in this high-risk population.

papers.title: Extreme phenotype-derived machine learning reveals susceptibility and resilience signatures for severe diabetic retinopathy.
papers.abstract: The mechanisms underlying why some individuals with diabetes develop severe diabetic retinopathy (DR), whereas others remain free of retinal complications despite long-standing disease, remain incompletely understood. We aimed to identify systemic susceptibility and resilience signatures associated with severe DR using an extreme phenotype-derived machine learning framework.
papers.summary: This study uses an extreme phenotype machine learning approach to identify systemic signatures that distinguish individuals with diabetes who develop severe diabetic retinopathy from those who remain resilient despite long-standing disease. The framework aims to uncover molecular or clinical features underlying susceptibility versus resilience to severe DR.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-driven prediction and design of cell-penetrating peptides for advanced drug delivery system.
papers.abstract: Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) are promising delivery vectors for transporting therapeutic agents across cellular membranes. However, their rational design remains challenging because the relationship between peptide sequence and translocation efficiency is highly complex and nonlinear.
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence approaches are being applied to predict and design cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) for drug delivery. It highlights that the complex, nonlinear relationship between peptide sequence and membrane translocation efficiency makes rational design difficult, motivating AI-driven methods as a promising solution.

papers.title: Advancing precision tacrolimus therapy: a systems genetics dissection in BXD platform.
papers.abstract: Tacrolimus is a core immunosuppressant in organ transplantation, but its narrow therapeutic window and significant pharmacokinetic variability hinder precision dosing. Although CYP3A5-guided strategies have established clinical relevance for tacrolimus initial dose adjustment, they do not fully account for the marked interindividual variability in tacrolimus exposure, highlighting the need for complementary models to decode more complex genetic regulation. This study aimed to identify candidate genetic modulators of tacrolimus metabolism and develop an integrated predictive framework for indiv
papers.summary: This study used the BXD mouse genetic reference panel to dissect the complex genetic regulation of tacrolimus pharmacokinetics beyond the known CYP3A5 pathway. The authors identified candidate genetic modulators of tacrolimus metabolism and built an integrated predictive framework aimed at improving individualized dosing. The work highlights the value of systems genetics for refining precision immunosuppressant therapy.

papers.title: Olink proteomics identifies serum protein biomarkers and an age-stratified diagnostic model for diabetes in Chinese patients.
papers.abstract: Aging is a critical risk factor for the progression and complications of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). However, routine clinical indicators fail to accurately quantify biological senescence burden in T2DM patients. This study aimed to screen plasma protein signatures associated with metabolic senescence in T2DM using Olink targeted proteomics and to construct a novel biological aging evaluation model for diabetic populations.
papers.summary: This study used Olink targeted proteomics to profile serum proteins in Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes, aiming to identify protein signatures linked to metabolic aging. The authors then built an age-stratified diagnostic model that incorporates these protein biomarkers to better evaluate biological senescence burden in diabetic populations. The work suggests that proteomic aging signatures could improve diagnosis and risk stratification beyond routine clinical indicators.
